title: Hope
tomorrow: can you pray 'please fix it' and 'whatever you want' at once?

cards: “I hope so,” about a job, a test result, a text that hasn't come back. In everyday talk, hope can sound like a coin tossed in a fountain. Here's an older picture.
Jacob has lost his son Joseph, and both the Bible and the Qur'an tell that story.
In the Qur'an's telling, Jacob, still grieving, sends his sons out to search for Joseph and his brother, and tells them not to despair of God's mercy. So what makes hope more than a wish?

teach.b: Paul answers with a ladder, in his letter to the Romans, and the bottom rung is trouble: “we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.”
Trouble, then patience, then tested character, then hope. Hope grows through hard things, not around them.
And it maketh not ashamed: it won't leave a person embarrassed for having held it, not because the odds are good, but because of a love already given.
Hebrews gives it a picture: “an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast.”
An anchor works out of sight, under the water, while the surface tosses. Now the neighbor.

teach.h: JACOB IN THE QUR'AN: DON'T DESPAIR.
teach.b: Muslims read Surah Yusuf, where Jacob tells his sons that only those who reject God despair of his mercy.
Christians and Muslims share this: hope that keeps searching in grief, rooted in God, not in luck. And one honest difference. Paul ties hope to the Holy Ghost poured into the heart, and to Christ.
Muslims honor Jesus as a prophet, not as God's Son, and the Qur'an roots Jacob's hope in God's mercy. Two scriptures, one grieving father, the same refusal to give up.

how: Christians speak of hope as resting on God's love and promises; in hard times they pray for one another, and some turn to Romans 5 and Hebrews 6.

o: a steady expectation of good that holds in trouble
a lucky wish that things will just work out
a prediction based on the odds being good

games.q: the ladder and the anchor — tap the pairs.

s: in Romans, Paul's path to hope starts with easy times
it starts with tribulation, then patience, then experience, then hope.
Jacob's grief for Joseph is told in the Qur'an as well as the Bible
Surah Yusuf tells it; there Jacob sends his sons to search and not to despair of God's mercy.
Hebrews calls hope an anchor of the soul
“an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast.”

games.q: your Muslim lab partner says her grandmother quotes Surah Yusuf when things look hopeless. what do you two honestly share?
o: hope that keeps searching in grief, rooted in God, not luck.
the exact same belief about Jesus and the Holy Spirit.
nothing at all; hope means something opposite in each.
games.why: both scriptures tell of Jacob refusing to despair. the honest difference: Paul ties hope to Christ and the Holy Ghost; the Qur'an roots it in God's mercy.

practice: Bring to mind one person going through something hard. Write them one short line of hope: not a prediction of how it will turn out, just that you're holding on for them. Send it, or keep it, and if you pray, pray for them by name.

wordCard.voice: Hope. A steady expectation of good that grows through trouble and holds, like an anchor out of sight.
